gaps.sentence: ___ mattered most was that nobody had been hurt.
gaps.explanation: 'What' = the thing that; it acts as subject of the clause.

gaps.sentence: The village ___ my grandmother was born has no shops.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' is the relative adverb for places; 'which' cannot stand alone here because no preposition is present.

gaps.sentence: I'll never forget the day ___ we first met.
gaps.explanation: 'When' replaces 'on which' after time nouns like day, year and moment.

gaps.sentence: It was the first time ___ I had ever driven on my own.
gaps.hint: after 'the first time', use this pronoun
gaps.explanation: 'The first time that ...' is the standard pattern; the pronoun may also be omitted, but 'which' and 'what' do not fit.

gaps.sentence: The chair on ___ the cat was sleeping was my grandmother's.
gaps.explanation: 'On which' is the formal pattern for things; 'on where' and 'on that' are not grammatical.

gaps.sentence: The train ___ leaves at six is usually very crowded.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' is the subject pronoun for things; the clause sits between the subject 'train' and its verb 'is'.
'What I meant' means 'the thing that I meant'; 'that I meant' would be an incomplete relative clause.

gaps.sentence: He passed all his exams first time, ___ surprised everyone.
gaps.hint: refers to the whole previous clause
gaps.explanation: 'Which' can refer to a whole idea ('he passed first time'); this non-defining use never takes 'that'.
